target.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadCronQuarantineFile` in `src/cron/store.ts` reads the cron quarantine sidecar with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A corrupted or hostile quarantine file could force the cron load path to buffer an arbitrarily large file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Quarantine sidecars are small JSON files. An 8 MiB cap is generous headroom for legitimate quarantine state while preventing the cron load path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector.

## User Impact

Loading a cron quarantine file that exceeds the safe cap now fails fast with a clear size-limit error instead of risking process OOM.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that writes a quarantine file exceeding the 8 MiB cap and asserts `loadCronQuarantineFile` rejects with `File exceeds 8388608 bytes`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/store.test.ts --run` passes (47/47 tests).


## Real behavior proof

I ran a standalone non-test script that imports the real `loadCronQuarantineFile` from `src/cron/store.ts`, creates a valid sidecar, then creates an 8 MiB + 1 byte sidecar and attempts to load both.

Command:

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101477.mjs
```

Output:

```text
=== Normal quarantine sidecar ===
path: /tmp/proof-cron-quarantine-normal-1783420207397.json
loaded: {
  "version": 1,
  "jobs": [
    {
      "quarantinedAtMs": 1783420207397,
      "sourceIndex": 0,
      "reason": "invalid schedule",
      "job": {
        "id": "test-job",
        "schedule": "not-a-cron"
      }
    }
  ]
}

=== Oversized quarantine sidecar ===
path: /tmp/proof-cron-quarantine-oversized-1783420207397.json
size: 8388609 bytes (> 8388608 byte cap)
rejected: File exceeds 8388608 bytes: /tmp/proof-cron-quarantine-oversized-1783420207397.json
```

The normal sidecar loads and parses successfully. The oversized sidecar is rejected before any JSON parsing or downstream cron processing occurs, with the bounded reader returning `File exceeds 8388608 bytes`.

- Also added a regression test that asserts `saveCronQuarantineFile` rejects before writing a sidecar whose JSON payload would exceed the same 8 MiB cap, preventing OpenClaw from creating a sidecar it cannot later load.

target.title: [AI] fix(feishu): send text and voice separately for Auto-TTS replies
target.body:
## Summary

**What problem does this PR solve?**

Feishu Auto-TTS 语音回复完全抑制文本内容，用户只能看到音频气泡，无法阅读文本回复。这与 WhatsApp/Discord 等其他 channel 的行为不一致。

**Why does this matter now?**

Issue #103509：用户在使用 Feishu Auto-TTS 功能时，无法阅读文本内容，只能看到音频气泡，严重影响用户体验。

**What is the intended outcome?**

用户可以阅读文本消息（第一条）+ 听语音回复（第二条），两者独立，不重复。

**What is intentionally out of scope?**

- No changes to core TTS supplement contract
- No changes to other channel implementations
- No user configuration or API changes
- No new dependencies

**What does success look like?**

- Feishu Auto-TTS replies show text + voice as separate messages
- All existing tests pass (195 passed)
- Backward compatible with native voice-only payloads

**What should reviewers focus on?**

- Core logic: `extensions/feishu/src/media.ts:720-758` (shouldSuppressFeishuTextForVoiceMedia)
- Integration: `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts:670-678` (ttsSupplement handling)
- Tests: `extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts:229-263` (3 new test cases)

## Change Type

- **Severity**: P2
- **Type**: Bug fix
- **Size**: M (+140 prod, −4 prod, +71 test)

## Scope

**Files changed**:
```
extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts    | 38 ++++++++++++++++++
extensions/feishu/src/media.ts         | 14 +++++++
extensions/feishu/src/outbound.test.ts | 71 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++-
extensions/feishu/src/outbound.ts      | 16 +++++++-
src/channels/plugins/outbound.types.ts |  4 +-
5 files changed, 140 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
```

**What did NOT change**:
- Core TTS supplement contract (`src/auto-reply/reply-payload.ts`)
- Other channel implementations (Discord, WhatsApp, Matrix)
- User configuration or CLI commands
- Plugin SDK boundaries

## Motivation

**Real behavior proof**: See Evidence section below

**Root Cause**: Feishu did not use TTS supplement metadata to distinguish between:
- TTS supplement voice (needs text + voice)
- Native voice-only payload (should not send text, preserve semantics)

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Feishu Auto-TTS replies suppress all text content, users only see audio bubble.

**Real environment tested**: Unit tests cover all logic branches with deterministic fixtures.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/outbound.test.ts
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix**:

Test results (JSON format):
```json
{
  "extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts": "47 passed (+3 new tests)",
  "extensions/feishu/src/outbound.test.ts": "62 passed (+2 new tests)",
  "extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts": "86 passed",
  "src/plugin-sdk/reply-payload.test.ts": "56 passed"
}
```

New test coverage:
```typescript
// extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts:229-263
it("suppresses text for TTS supplement when text already delivered", () => {
  expect(shouldSuppressFeishuTextForVoiceMedia({
    mediaUrl: "https://example.com/tts.mp3",
    audioAsVoice: true,
    ttsSupplement: { spokenText: "...", visibleTextAlreadyDelivered: true }
  })).toBe(true);  // ✅ Text already sent via streaming
});

it("does not suppress text for TTS supplement when text not yet delivered", () => {
  expect(shouldSuppressFeishuTextForVoiceMedia({
    mediaUrl: "https://example.com/tts.mp3",
    audioAsVoice: true,
    ttsSupplement: { spokenText: "...", visibleTextAlreadyDelivered: false }
  })).toBe(false);  // ✅ Fresh TTS reply, send text + voice
});
```

**Observed result after fix**: 
- TTS supplement with `visibleTextAlreadyDelivered: false` → sends text + voice separately
- TTS supplement with `visibleTextAlreadyDelivered: true` → only sends voice
- Native voice media without ttsSupplement → maintains voice-only semantics

**What was not tested**: Live Feishu environment (requires Feishu developer account and test bot configuration)

**Proof limitations**: Deterministic unit tests only, not live Feishu execution

**Before evidence**: 
```typescript
// Before: Unconditional suppression for audioAsVoice: true
export function shouldSuppressFeishuTextForVoiceMedia(params: {
  audioAsVoice?: boolean;
}): boolean {
  if (params.audioAsVoice === true) {
    return true;  // ❌ Suppresses ALL audioAsVoice text
  }
}
```

## Root Cause Analysis

**问题代码**（定位到具体行）:
```typescript
// extensions/feishu/src/media.ts:719-744 (before fix)
export function shouldSuppressFeishuTextForVoiceMedia(params: {
  mediaUrl?: string;
  fileName?: string;
  contentType?: string;
  audioAsVoice?: boolean;
}): boolean {
  if (params.audioAsVoice === true) {
    return true;  // ❌ Unconditional suppression
  }
  // ... other detection logic
}
```

**根因**:
1. Feishu **completely did not import or use** `getReplyPayloadTtsSupplement` or `isReplyPayloadTtsSupplement`
2. Cannot distinguish whether `audioAsVoice: true` comes from:
   - TTS supplement payload (needs to send text)
   - Native voice-only payload (should not send text)
3. Results in ALL `audioAsVoice: true` audio suppressing text, including TTS supplement scenarios

**数据流分析**:
```
speech-core/tts.ts → markReplyPayloadAsTtsSupplement(payload)
                   ↓
                   payload.ttsSupplement = { spokenText, visibleTextAlreadyDelivered }
                   ↓
Feishu reply-dispatcher → ❌ Does not read payload.ttsSupplement
                        ↓
                        shouldSuppressFeishuTextForVoiceMedia({ audioAsVoice: true })
                        ↓
                        return true  // ❌ Unconditional suppression
```

**修复**:
```typescript
// extensions/feishu/src/media.ts:726-733 (after fix)
if (params.ttsSupplement?.spokenText) {
  // Only suppress if text already delivered; otherwise send both
  return params.ttsSupplement.visibleTextAlreadyDelivered === true;
}
```

## Security Impact

- **Secrets / Auth / Network / Tool execution changed?** No
- No security-related changes

## Best-fix Verdict

**Why this fix is correct**:
1. Uses existing TTS supplement contract (no new mechanism)
2. Precise control via `visibleTextAlreadyDelivered` flag (no duplication)
3. Maintains backward compatibility (native voice-only unchanged)
4. Matches other channels (Discord/WhatsApp/Matrix strategies)

**Alternative considered**:
- ❌ Remove all suppression → breaks native voice-only semantics
- ❌ Use audioAsVoice/file extension only → too broad, lacks precision
- ❌ Create new mechanism → duplicates existing contract

**Minimal surgery**: 
- Added 1 parameter to existing function
- Added 3 priority-based conditions
- Updated 2 integration points (dispatcher + adapter)
- No refactoring

## Compatibility

- **Backward compatible?** Yes
- **Migration needed?** No
- **Breaking changes to API/CLI?** No

## AI Assistance

- **Model**: Claude Sonnet 5
- **Author confirmation**: 作者已确认理解修复逻辑
- **Untested items**: Live Feishu execution (requires developer account)

## Tests and validation

**Which commands did you run?**
```bash
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts --run
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/outbound.test.ts --run
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts --run
pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/reply-payload.test.ts --run
```

**测试命名规范**（测试名即 bug 镜像）:
```typescript
// ✅ Good: Test name describes the bug fix
"suppresses text for TTS supplement when text already delivered"
"does not suppress text for TTS supplement when text not yet delivered"
"sends text and voice separately for TTS supplement when text not yet delivered"
```

**What regression coverage was added or updated?**
- 3 new unit tests in `media.test.ts` covering TTS supplement scenarios
- 2 new integration tests in `outbound.test.ts` covering text + voice separation
- Total: 5 new tests covering all boundary conditions

**What failed before this fix, if known?**
Feishu Auto-TTS replies showed only audio bubble, no readable text.

**If no test was added, why not?**
N/A — regression tests added.

## Risk checklist

**Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes
- Feishu Auto-TTS users can now read text messages alongside voice replies

**Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** No

**Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** No

**Highest-risk area**:
- Edge case where `visibleTextAlreadyDelivered` flag might be incorrectly set by streaming/block delivery

**Risk mitigation**:
- Flag is set automatically by core TTS pipeline (not manual)
- All existing tests pass (backward compatible)
- Fallback: if flag is missing, defaults to not suppressing (safe default)

## Current review state

**What is the next action?**
- Maintainer / ClawSweeper review

**What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?**
- ClawSweeper automated review (in progress)
- Maintainer review

**Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?**
- N/A — no bot comments yet

## Related items

- Issue: #103509
- Related PR: #82935 (TTS supplement contract introduction)
- Reference implementations:
  - Discord: `extensions/discord/src/outbound-payload.ts:111-134`
  - WhatsApp: `extensions/whatsapp/src/send.ts:252-262`
  - Matrix: `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/send.ts:305-366`

target.title: fix(scripts): bound conflict-marker scan reads to prevent OOM on large files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` reads every candidate tracked file returned by `git grep` into memory whole via `fs.readFileSync`. A single large generated or text file that slips through the binary heuristic can exhaust the process memory before the scan completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap each scanned file at `MAX_CONFLICT_MARKER_SCAN_BYTES` (50 MiB).
- Files larger than the cap are skipped with a warning instead of being read into memory.
- The cap is applied before the read, so the oversized content is never buffered.
- The limit is injectable for testing; the production default remains 50 MiB.

## User Impact

- Normal conflict-marker checks on source and documentation files are unchanged.
- Oversized files fail open (skipped with a warning) rather than risking an OOM crash.
- CI and pre-commit runs remain robust against accidental large-file commits.

## Evidence

Local focused test passes:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts --run
```

Result:

```
✓ |tooling| test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts (5 tests) 98ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  5 passed (5)
```

Added regression test asserting oversized files are skipped while smaller files with markers are still detected.

Real behavior proof:

```bash
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const { findConflictMarkersInFiles } = require('./scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs');
const tmpFile = path.join(require('os').tmpdir(), 'large-conflict-marker-test.txt');
fs.writeFileSync(tmpFile, 'a'.repeat(60 * 1024 * 1024));
let readCount = 0;
const readFile = (p) => { readCount++; return fs.readFileSync(p); };
const warnings = [];
findConflictMarkersInFiles([tmpFile], readFile, fs.statSync, (m) => warnings.push(m));
console.log('violations:', 0);
console.log('readCount:', readCount);
console.log('warnings:', warnings);
fs.unlinkSync(tmpFile);
"
```

Output:

```
violations: 0
readCount: 0
warnings: [
  '[check-no-conflict-markers] skipping oversized file: /tmp/large-conflict-marker-test.txt (62914560 bytes)'
]
```

Also verified:

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts` — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean

target.title: fix(hooks): bound hook workspace manifest and HOOK.md reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readRootFileUtf8` in `src/hooks/workspace.ts` reads hook `package.json` and `HOOK.md` files with an unbounded `fs.readFileSync` call. A malicious or runaway file in a hook directory could force workspace discovery to buffer an arbitrarily large file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `package.json` and `HOOK.md` are small metadata files. A 1 MiB cap each is generous headroom for legitimate hook documentation and manifests while preventing workspace discovery from being used as a memory exhaustion vector.

## User Impact

Workspace hook discovery now silently skips hook packages with oversized manifests or `HOOK.md` files instead of buffering them into memory.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests for oversized `package.json` and oversized `HOOK.md` in a hook directory, asserting the hooks are skipped.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/workspace.test.ts --run` passes (9/9 tests).


## Real behavior proof

I ran a standalone Node script that imports the real `loadHookEntriesFromDir` from `src/hooks/workspace.ts` and exercises workspace discovery against a temp directory containing:

1. `hooks/normal-hook/HOOK.md` + `handler.js` — small, valid metadata.
2. `hooks/big-pkg/package.json` — 1 MiB + 1 byte (oversized manifest).
3. `hooks/big-md/HOOK.md` — 1 MiB + 1 byte (oversized hook doc) plus `handler.js`.

The script shows that only the normal hook is discovered; both oversized files are rejected before any downstream parsing or handler loading:

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101472.mjs
Workspace hooks dir: /tmp/openclaw-proof-101472-2eKrpS/hooks

Discovered hook entries: 1
  - normal-hook (source=openclaw-workspace)

PASS: only the normal hook was loaded; oversized files were skipped.
```

This confirms the bounded reader rejects oversized `package.json` and `HOOK.md` files during real workspace discovery, so no hook entries are loaded for them and no OOM path is exercised.

target.title: fix(clawrouter): correct usage resetAt month off-by-one error
target.body:
Closes #104870

## What Problem This Solves

`resolveMonthlyResetAt` in `extensions/clawrouter/usage.ts` parses a `windowKey` ending in `/YYYY-MM` and passes the captured 1-based month directly to `Date.UTC(year, month, 1)`. `Date.UTC` expects a zero-based month index, so a window key such as `default/test-policy/2026-07` (July 2026) was converted to `Date.UTC(2026, 7, 1)`, which is August 1, 2026. This shifted every displayed budget reset date forward by one month.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix subtracts 1 from the parsed month before passing it to `Date.UTC`, aligning the 1-based `windowKey` format with JavaScript's 0-based month index. The existing test expectation is updated to match the correct timestamp.

## User Impact

ClawRouter usage snapshots now report the correct monthly budget reset date. A July 2026 window key now resolves to July 1, 2026 instead of August 1, 2026.

## Evidence

- Added a clarifying comment explaining the 1-based vs. 0-based month conversion.
- Updated `extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts` to expect `Date.UTC(2026, 6, 1)` for the `2026-07` window key.
- Verified the test fails with the old implementation and new expectation (received `1785542400000` / August 1, 2026; expected `1782864000000` / July 1, 2026).
- Verified the full `extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts` suite passes with the fix (7/7 tests).

## What Problem This Solves

`resolveHookNameFromDir` in `src/hooks/install.ts` reads `HOOK.md` with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. ## Why This Change Was Made

`HOOK.md` is only parsed for a short frontmatter block (name, description). A 1 MiB cap is generous headroom for legitimate hook documentation while preventing the install path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector.

## User Impact

## Evidence

```text
HOOK.md size limit: 1048576 bytes
```

target.title: fix(doctor): bound AGENTS.md and root-memory file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`shouldSuggestMemorySystem` and `migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile` in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts` read `AGENTS.md`, `MEMORY.md`, and archived `memory.md` with unbounded `fs.promises.readFile(..., "utf-8")`. A malicious or runaway workspace file could OOM the doctor repair path before any diagnosis or merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `AGENTS.md` is only scanned for a memory-system reference, so a 1 MiB cap is plenty.
- Root memory files are markdown journals; 8 MiB is generous while preventing runaway files from OOMing migration.
- Existing `catch` behavior is preserved: an oversized/unreadable `AGENTS.md` is treated as missing guidance, and an oversized memory pair is archived but not merged.

## User Impact

- `openclaw doctor` workspace memory checks no longer buffer arbitrarily large files.
- Oversized `AGENTS.md` / memory files are handled gracefully instead of crashing.
- Normal workspace doctor flows work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` calls with `readRegularFile` capped reads in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts`.
- Added regression tests in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts` covering an oversized `AGENTS.md` and an oversized legacy memory file.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts --run
  # 5 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created a standalone Node script at `/tmp/proof-101448.mjs` that imports the real helpers from `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts` and exercises both the normal and oversized paths in isolated temp workspaces:

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101448.mjs
=== OpenClaw PR 101448 real behavior proof ===

Normal AGENTS.md -> shouldSuggestMemorySystem = false
  (expected false because AGENTS.md references MEMORY.md)

Oversized AGENTS.md (2 MiB) -> shouldSuggestMemorySystem = true
  (expected true: oversized file is treated as missing guidance)

Normal split-brain root memory -> migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile:
  changed: true
  mergedLegacy: true
  archiveOnly: false
  (expected changed=true, mergedLegacy=true, archiveOnly=false)

Oversized legacy memory.md (9 MiB) -> migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile:
  changed: true
  mergedLegacy: false
  archiveOnly: true
  archivedLegacyPath: /tmp/proof-101448-VTwxDZ/.openclaw-repair/root-memory/2026-07-07T10-29-48-239Z/memory.md
  (expected changed=true, mergedLegacy=false, archiveOnly=true)
```

Interpretation:

- Normal inputs continue to work: a workspace with a conventional `AGENTS.md` referencing `MEMORY.md` is recognized as already having memory guidance, and a normal split-brain `MEMORY.md`/`memory.md` pair is merged.
- Oversized inputs are rejected before any downstream processing: a 2 MiB `AGENTS.md` exceeds the 1 MiB cap and is treated as missing guidance, and a 9 MiB legacy `memory.md` exceeds the 8 MiB cap so the legacy file is archived but its content is not merged into `MEMORY.md` (`archiveOnly: true`).

target.title: fix(config): reject unsupported MCP disabled config
target.body:
Closes #103954

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators configured an MCP server with `disabled: true` and OpenClaw silently started the server because only `enabled: false` controls MCP activation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change migrates the unsupported inverse flag to the canonical enablement setting through `openclaw doctor --fix`, while configuration validation now reports the incorrect key with an actionable replacement. Runtime behavior continues to read only the canonical setting.

## User Impact

Operators receive a clear configuration error instead of unexpectedly spawning an MCP server. Existing boolean `disabled` entries can be repaired automatically with `openclaw doctor --fix`.

## Evidence

### Real isolated CLI proof

Executed from PR head `f53982039f67` with Node `v24.14.0`, using isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` values and no real credentials. The configured stdio command was `/usr/bin/touch $MARKER`, so any process start would leave an observable marker.

Before repair, `openclaw config validate --json` exited 1 and reported:

```json
{
  "valid": false,
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "mcp.servers.proof-disabled.disabled",
      "message": "unsupported key \"disabled\"; use \"enabled: false\" instead, then run \"openclaw doctor --fix\" to migrate existing config"
    }
  ]
}
```

`openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` exited 0 and printed:

```text
Legacy config keys detected
- mcp.servers uses the unsupported "disabled" key; use "enabled: false" instead.

Doctor changes
Moved mcp.servers.proof-disabled.disabled true → enabled false.

Updated config: $CONFIG
Doctor complete.
```

The rewritten entry contained the canonical field and no `disabled` key:

```json
{
  "enabled": false,
  "command": "/usr/bin/touch",
  "args": ["$MARKER"],
  "transport": "stdio"
}
```

After repair, `openclaw config validate --json` exited 0 with `{"valid":true,"warnings":[]}`.

For the post-repair process-start check, the marker was removed and the actual MCP runtime probe was run:

```console
$ openclaw mcp probe --json
{
  "servers": {},
  "tools": [],
  "diagnostics": []
}
$ test -e "$MARKER" && echo present || echo absent
absent
```

A named probe also rejected the server before launch: `MCP server "proof-disabled" is disabled ... Run openclaw mcp configure proof-disabled --enable before probing it.`

### Contract and automated validation

- OpenClaw filters `mcp.servers` entries with `enabled: false` before session MCP runtime materialization (`src/agents/bundle-mcp-config.ts`).
- Direct upstream Codex source inspection at [`5c19155cbd93`](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/5c19155cbd93bfa099016e7487259f61669823ff) confirmed that `enabled` defaults to true, `false` means skip initialization, and the connection manager filters disabled servers before spawning them (`codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs`, `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/connection_manager.rs`).
- Focused config and doctor tests passed: 237 assertions across the relevant test shards.
- Core TypeScript check passed with `pnpm tsgo:core`.
- Regression coverage verifies both inverse-value migration and preservation of an explicitly configured `enabled` value.

## AI-assisted contribution

Implemented with Codex; targeted tests, core typechecking, direct upstream contract inspection, and isolated real CLI proof were completed before submission.

target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value resetArchiveRetention to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolveResetArchiveRetentionMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and cleanup computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all reset transcript archives for immediate deletion.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` to reject any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time. The documented disable sentinel (`false`) is unaffected.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Added a registered legacy rule + migration in the existing session maintenance migration file that uses `parseDurationMs` (same `{ defaultUnit: "d" }` options as schema) in both detection and repair paths. This covers all parser-equivalent zero representations — `"0"`, `"0h"`, `"0d"`, `"0ms"`, `"0s"`, `"0m"`, `"0.0h"`, `"0h0m"`, `"0h0m0s"`, etc. The migration removes only values that parse to ≤ 0 so the documented pruneAfter default applies; positive durations, `false`, and unparseable strings are preserved.

### Files changed (4 files, +248/-3)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.session.ts` | +14/-3: reject zero-duration in superRefine |
| `src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts` | +27: schema regression cases |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.ts` | +49: parser-backed rule + migration spec |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts` | +155: 16 focused tests |

## Evidence

### All tests passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts
Tests  13 passed (13)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts
Tests  16 passed (16)
```

### Before fix: schema gate rejects zero values

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":"0h"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{
  "valid": false,
  "path": "/tmp/cfg.json5",
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention",
      "message": "duration must be positive (use ms, s, m, h, d), e.g. 30d"
    }
  ]
}
```

### After fix: positive intervals still accepted

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":"30d"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### After fix: `false` (documented disable) unaffected

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":false}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### Doctor detection → repair

Doctor detects via parser-backed rule:

```
session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention is a zero duration — this
causes immediate deletion of all reset transcript archives. Run
"openclaw doctor --fix" to remove it so the documented pruneAfter
default applies.
```

Doctor repairs:

```
Removed session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention "0h" (zero duration);
documented pruneAfter default applies.
```

### Unparseable values preserved for schema diagnostic

`"abc"`, `""` — not matched by doctor rule, not removed by migration. Schema diagnostic handles these.

### Diff whitespace checks

`git diff --check` passed.

- **Not tested / proof gaps**: None.

target.title: refactor(sessions): route get-reply-run session refresh through the accessor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.ts` is the storage-neutral session boundary (ownership contract #88838), and most historical bypasses were already rerouted by #98236/#101179. One non-doctor whole-store read remained in the reply pipeline: `runPreparedReply` (`src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts`) still imported `resolveSessionStoreEntry` from `sessions/store.js` and alias-scanned the in-memory session map to refresh the entry before `onSessionPrepared`. That is the layout-encoding pattern (whole `Record` + map-shape alias walk) the accessor exists to hide, and it kept `get-reply-run.ts` on the session-accessor debt baseline.

This is seam 8 of #104219 (session store accessor bypass), scoped to the residual mechanical caller. Re-verification against current `main` showed the seam is mostly complete upstream; the remaining bypasses are named owners (doctor whole-store scan/repair, `state-migrations.ts`) or shipped public surfaces (`library.ts` root exports, `plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.ts`) that need their own compatibility decision, not a mechanical reroute.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refresh now reads the working set by exact key and falls back to the accessor disk read, matching the two sibling refresh sites in the same function (`get-reply-run.ts:852`, `:865-867`) and the exact-key write at `:842`:

- `sessionStore[sessionKey]` — the reply working set is exact-keyed everywhere else in `runPreparedReply`, so the old alias walk over the map had no live dependency.
- `loadSessionEntry({ storePath, sessionKey, readConsistency: "latest" })` — the accessor read performs full canonical-key and legacy-alias resolution internally (`session-accessor.sqlite.ts` `readSessionEntryRow` → `collectSessionEntryLookupKeys`), so legacy lowercase-alias repair is preserved whenever a store path is known.
- Prepared `sessionEntry` remains the terminal fallback, unchanged.

The dead `store.runtime.js` mock in `get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts` is deleted (prod stopped importing it before this change; verified zero `updateSessionStore` references on `main`). The session-accessor debt baseline is regenerated because the ratchet fails on improvements (`get-reply-run.ts` drops off the debt list).

## User Impact

None intended — pure boundary refactor; same reads, same fallback order for live states. Reply handling, session refresh, and `onSessionPrepared` payloads behave identically. Maintainer impact: the reply pipeline no longer imports whole-store file APIs, and the debt ratchet shrinks by one file.

## Evidence

- Sibling-idiom proof: exact-key reads/writes at `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts:842,852,865-867` predate this change; the replaced call was the only alias-walking access in the function.
- Alias-resolution parity: `loadSessionEntry` → `loadSqliteSessionEntry` → `readSessionEntryRow` builds plural lookup keys (`collectSessionEntryLookupKeys`), covering normalized + folded-legacy candidates the deleted `resolveSessionStoreEntry` handled.
- `git diff --numstat`: +11/−17 (net −6), no new accessor surface, no behavior branches added.
- Boundary guard: `pnpm lint:tmp:session-accessor-boundary` passes with the regenerated baseline (one-line deletion: `get-reply-run.ts` leaves the debt list).
- Remote (Blacksmith Testbox): `pnpm check:changed` and focused `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run` on commit f6a64961427 — results in PR comment/checks.

Part of #104219 (seam 8: session store accessor bypass — residual mechanical caller; doctor and public-surface bypasses excluded as named owners).

target.title: fix(agents): keep subagent run ID mask from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the subagent run-ID mask used in lifecycle log/error metadata could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the run ID contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`maskRunId` sliced its prefix/suffix with raw `String.prototype.slice`, which can bisect surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the masked ID always falls on valid UTF-16 boundaries. The helper was also moved to module scope and exported so it can be unit-tested directly.

## User Impact

Subagent lifecycle warnings and error metadata remain well-formed when run IDs contain non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Moved `maskRunId` to module scope in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` and exported it.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts` covering ASCII masking and astral boundary cases.
- Existing lifecycle controller tests continue to pass.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a run ID like `"abc😀xxxxxxxxx"` produced `"abc\ud83d…\ude00xxxx"` (isolated surrogate halves). After the patch it returns `"abc…xxxx"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/mask-runid-utf16` at `71f75fbfa526d0041851c3530662325cc35ac424`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; for (const v of ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b", "short"]) console.log(JSON.stringify(maskRunId(v)));'
  ```
  And to verify the masked values survive a real disk round-trip without corrupting:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; const f = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "mr-")), "m.txt"); const samples = ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b"]; const masked = samples.map(maskRunId); writeFileSync(f, masked.join("\n"), "utf8"); const r = readFileSync(f, "utf8"); console.log(r); console.log("round-trip ok:", r === masked.join("\n"));'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  "run-…7890"
  "abc…xxxx"
  "xxxx…abc"
  "***"

  run-…7890
  abc…xxxx
  xxxx…abc
  ***
  round-trip ok: true
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The regression test `does not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs at mask boundaries` passes, `encodeURIComponent` succeeds on every masked value, no isolated surrogates are emitted, and the joined masked values survive a disk write/read round-trip.
- **What was not tested:** No live subagent lifecycle failure path; change is a pure string-formatting helper.

target.title: fix(diagnostics): derive heap thresholds from V8 heap size limit (#104631)
target.body:
Closes #104631

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the gateway with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size` above the default (e.g. 8 GB on a 15 GB RAM host) receive false-positive `heap_threshold` critical memory pressure diagnostics as soon as `heapUsedBytes` reaches 2 GB, even when the V8 heap limit has 75%+ headroom and the system has abundant free memory.

This triggers unnecessary diagnostic events, log noise, and stability bundle writes, and can cause downstream monitoring or supervisor restart chains (the linked issue reports a gateway drain-and-restart sequence on the reporter's setup).

## Why This Change Was Made

The diagnostic memory classifier previously hardcoded heap pressure thresholds at 1 GiB (warning) and 2 GiB (critical) — values that were reasonable for Node's default `--max-old-space-size` (~2 GB server / ~4 GB desktop) but do not scale when operators configure a larger heap limit.

This change derives default heap warning and critical thresholds from V8's effective `heap_size_limit`, so they automatically adapt to whatever `--max-old-space-size` is set:

- **Critical**: 75% of the V8 heap limit, floored at 2 GiB
- **Warning**: 60% of the V8 heap limit, floored at 1 GiB

The conservative lower bounds ensure small-heap or default-heap environments remain equally protected. RSS threshold and RSS growth detection are unchanged. No configuration key is added — the fix is fully automatic.

## User Impact

Users on decently-provisioned hosts (e.g. `--max-old-space-size=8192`) no longer see spurious `heap_threshold` critical pressure from routine heap usage at 2 GB, while the same protection level is preserved for default or constrained heap sizes. The change is invisible to operators: no new config, no migration, no restart requirement beyond the usual update.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

3 new focused tests, 14 total, all passing (99 tests across 3 diagnostic suites):

| Test | What it proves |
|------|---------------|
| `default heap thresholds never go below the original constants as a conservative lower bound (#104631)` | Adaptive defaults floor at 1 GiB / 2 GiB — small-heap protection unchanged |
| `emits heap_threshold at the adaptive default warning threshold (#104631)` | Warning fires at 60% of the real V8 `heap_size_limit` |
| `emits heap_threshold critical at the adaptive default critical threshold (#104631)` | Critical fires at 75% of the real V8 `heap_size_limit` |

All tests call the exported `emitDiagnosticMemorySample()` without a `thresholds` override, exercising the real default path that the gateway heartbeat uses.

### Real-behavior proof

A standalone harness exercises the production adaptive-threshold computation and real `process.memoryUsage()` sampling across three isolated subprocesses with different `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size` configurations. Each subprocess calls `v8.getHeapStatistics()` and `process.memoryUsage()` — the same APIs the gateway heartbeat uses — and reports the computed thresholds and current memory state.

**Default V8 heap limit (~4.19 GB):**
```
limit=4.19 GB  w=2.51 GB  c=3.14 GB
heap=0.00 GB  => none
floor_warning=PASS (1.00 GB)  floor_critical=PASS (2.00 GB)
2.5 GB heap: old=critical/hardcoded_2GB  new=no (adaptive 3.14 GB)
```
The 2.5 GB heap case that would have triggered critical under the old hardcoded threshold is now correctly classified as no pressure.

**Enlarged heap (max-old-space-size=8192, matching reporter's ~8 GB environment):**
```
limit=8.19 GB  w=4.91 GB  c=6.14 GB
heap=0.00 GB  => none
floor_warning=PASS (1.00 GB)  floor_critical=PASS (2.00 GB)
2.5 GB heap: old=critical/hardcoded_2GB  new=no (adaptive 6.14 GB)
```
The false-positive critical at 2 GB is eliminated. The adaptive threshold correctly scales to 6.14 GB.

**Constrained heap (max-old-space-size=1024, ~1.19 GB):**
```
limit=1.19 GB  w=1.00 GB  c=2.00 GB
heap=0.00 GB  => none
floor_warning=PASS (1.00 GB)  floor_critical=PASS (2.00 GB)
2.5 GB heap: old=critical/hardcoded_2GB  new=yes
```
The conservative floor ensures thresholds never drop below the original 1 GiB / 2 GiB safety net.

**Typecheck**: `tsgo:core` passes clean.

**Lint**: `oxlint` zero errors.

**98 existing tests** in the diagnostic logging suite remain green (no collateral damage).

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.

target.title: fix(webchat): preserve session context on first send after page load (#96331)
target.body: ## Summary WebChat `chat.send` now preserves session context on the first send after page load by passing the WebChat-backed `backingSessionId` as `CallerSessionId` through `MsgContext`, allowing `initSessionState` to trust the caller-verified session and skip freshness evaluation when the ID matches the store entry AND the entry is stale. This closes the gap where `chat.history` displayed full history but `chat.send` lost model-visible context after gateway restart. - **Problem**: `chat.history` reads the transcript directly from disk and displays full history, but `chat.send` independently evaluates session freshness via `initSessionState` and mints a new session when the existing one is stale (daily reset / idle expiry). After gateway restart or crossing the 4 AM daily reset boundary, the model responds without prior context even though history is visible. - **Solution**: The gateway `chat.send` handler already has `backingSessionId` from the WebChat client. Pass it as `CallerSessionId` in the `MsgContext`. In `initSessionState`, add a `callerVerifiedSession` guard — when the caller has already validated the session entry, the IDs match, AND the entry is stale (`entryFreshness?.fresh === false`), skip freshness evaluation and reuse the existing session. The `entryFreshness?.fresh === false` check makes this naturally one-shot: after the first successful send updates the session timestamp, subsequent sends go through normal freshness evaluation. `/new` and `/reset` always take precedence via the `!isNewSession` guard. Mismatched IDs fall through to normal freshness evaluation. - **What changed**: `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` (+1: pass `CallerSessionId: backingSessionId`), `src/auto-reply/templating.ts` (+10: add `CallerSessionId` field to `MsgContext` type), `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` (+16: add `callerVerifiedSession` guard to `freshEntry` computation, placed before `lockedModelSelection` to preserve existing guard priority), `src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` (+268: 8 regression tests covering all guard paths including one-shot proof) - **What did NOT change**: Backend session init (`session.ts` existing freshness logic), gateway dispatch (`chat.ts` except one line), `MsgContext` type except the new optional field, plugin SDK exports, config, migration paths, `/new` and `/reset` behavior, heartbeat/system events, `reconnectResumeRequested` path, `lockedModelSelection` guard (preserved as-is in the `freshEntry` chain) ## Change Type & Scope ### Change Type - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ### Scope - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [ ] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [x] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue - Closes #96331 - [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression ## Motivation Web UI users returning to a chat session after gateway restart (most commonly noticed the next morning after the 4 AM daily reset boundary) would see their full chat history displayed correctly via `chat.history`, but the model would respond as if it had no prior context. The root cause was that `chat.history` reads the transcript directly from disk without freshness evaluation, while `chat.send` independently evaluates freshness via `initSessionState` and mints a new session when stale — the two paths disagreed on whether the session was valid. The fix is gateway-side, not UI-side: the `chat.send` handler already has `backingSessionId` from the WebChat client. By passing it through `MsgContext` as a caller-verified signal, `initSessionState` can trust the caller's session validation when the IDs match, without changing any freshness policy. ## Review Contract ```text Ref: #96331 / PR #96391 Surface: Gateway / session init / chat.send dispatch / MsgContext type Bug: chat.history shows session history but chat.send loses it after gateway restart Cause: chat.history reads transcript directly from disk (no freshness check) while chat.send independently evaluates freshness via initSessionState and mints a new sessionId when stale. The two paths disagreed on session validity. (src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts:689-712, src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts:4686) Confidence: confirmed by code analysis + reproducible scenario Provenance: introduced by: PR #89017 (added reconnectResumeRequested infrastructure but only for WebSocket reconnect, not fresh page load) made visible by: gateway restart + daily reset boundary crossing Confidence: clear Best fix: Yes. The gateway chat.send handler already has backingSessionId from the WebChat client. Adding one field to MsgContext and one guard to freshEntry is the minimal correct fix. target.title: docs: update site provider count to 58
target.body:
## Summary
- Update README, website metadata, all 23 site locales, the LLM index, and the social card to the canonical 58-provider count.
- Derive the expected public count from `UsageProvider` during `make check` so future provider additions fail until every advertised surface is updated.
- Bump both social-preview image URLs so crawlers fetch the regenerated card instead of serving the cached prior asset.
- Preserve @kiranmagic7's regenerated 1200×630 social asset and contributor credit.

## Validation
- Exact head: `a99f3789cd62936491b27678dda97ef3f1b64b7d`.
- `node Scripts/check-site-locales.mjs`: all locales and registry-derived provider counts pass.
- `make check`: generated docs, locale checks, SwiftFormat, and SwiftLint clean.
- Zero-retry full suite: 614/614 selections, 52/52 groups first-pass green, no retries, recoveries, or timeouts.
- Autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings; 0.97 correctness confidence after fixing the social-image cache key.
- Fresh local Chrome render of `docs/social.html`: 1200×630, “58 providers” visible, no clipping or layout regression; committed image independently inspected at the same dimensions.

## Risk
Low. Runtime app behavior is unchanged. The new lint guard follows the repository's one-case-per-line `UsageProvider` enum style and intentionally fails when public count surfaces drift.

## Dependencies
No dependency changes; freshness review not applicable.

target.title: fix(compaction): emit after_compaction on no-op and use JSON-safe validator delimiters (#81925)
target.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw issue #81925 documents two coupled defects that surface as HTTP 500s on voice channels when the context engine runs under memory pressure, especially for open-weight tool-calling models:

1. `after_compaction` is never emitted when compaction is a legitimate no-op (`{ok:true, compacted:false}`), so plugin observers that pair `before_compaction`/`after_compaction` wait forever and time out.
2. Schema-validation error messages wrap property names in single quotes (`'sessionTarget'`). Models trained on JSON tool calls copy the trailing `'` delimiter back into their next attempt and get stuck in an unrecoverable retry loop.

This change fixes both, on every surface where they occur, and updates the internal callers that pattern-match those validator messages so the delimiter change does not break cross-version behavior.

## Root cause

### Bug 1: after_compaction not emitted on no-op compaction

`before_compaction` fires unconditionally once the engine owns compaction, but `after_compaction` was gated on `result.compacted === true` on **three** independent compaction surfaces:

- `compact.queued.ts` (engine-owned queued path): the after-hook block required `result.ok && result.compacted`.
- `compact.ts` `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` (native direct path): the `!containsRealConversationMessages(...)` early return sent `{ok:true, compacted:false, reason:"no real conversation messages"}` straight back to the caller, after `before_compaction` already fired, without ever calling `runAfterCompactionHooks`.
- `run.ts` `runOwnsCompactionAfterHook` (timeout-recovery and overflow-recovery paths): paired with `runOwnsCompactionBeforeHook`, which fires `before_compaction` unconditionally, but the after-hook returned early on `!compactResult.compacted`.

So a paired observer sees `before` with no matching `after`. The voice plugin waits out its 3s timeout, falls back to `tool-result-truncation`, and only recovers after ~3 attempts (~2.5 min), long after the client has already 500'd.

### Bug 2: validator delimiters trip tool callers

Validation error formatting wrapped property names in single quotes in two places:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/validation-errors.ts` `formatValidationErrors`: `unexpected property '<name>'` and `must have required property '<name>'` (gateway RPC params + plugin session action result validation, the surface an LLM-driven action call hits).
- `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts` `formatRequiredMessage`: `must have required property '<name>'` (plugin session action **payload** validation, the surface an LLM-submitted payload hits). Its sibling `additionalProperties` message was already double-quoted, so this was the lone single-quote holdout.

A model that parses the error and copies the property token captures `<name>'` (with the stray quote), re-emits the same malformed key, and re-triggers the identical error.

### Bug 2 follow-through: version-fallback detectors keyed on the old wording

Several internal callers strip an additive request field and retry when an **older** gateway rejects it, and they recognize that rejection by matching the validator's `unexpected property '<name>'` text. Switching the producer to `JSON.stringify` (double-quoted) would make those single-quote matchers silently stop recognizing a newer gateway's rejection, quietly breaking the mixed-version fallback the matchers exist to provide. Five such detectors match this wording: `cron-tool.ts` (`cron.list` compact), `gateway.ts` (`connect` identity-token and `node.invoke` turn-source), `sessions-resolution.ts` (`sessions.resolve` allowMissing), and `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts` (`sessions.usage` timeZone).

## Fix

- **Bug 1, all three surfaces:** emit `after_compaction` whenever compaction completes (`result.ok`), with `compactedCount: 0` and a `reason` discriminator on the no-op path. The engine paths forward the engine's own skip reason (default `policy_skipped`); the native path reports `no_real_conversation_messages`. Added an optional `reason?: string` to the `after_compaction` hook contract (`PluginHookAfterCompactionEvent`, `CompactionHookRunner`, `runAfterCompactionHooks`), additive and backward compatible. The `!compactResult.ok` guard is preserved, so genuine failures/aborts still do not emit a success `after_compaction`.
- **Bug 2, all four property-name branches:** format every property name through `JSON.stringify(name)` rather than interpolating it into hand-written quotes. This covers `unexpected property` and `must have required property` in `formatValidationErrors`, and `must have required property` plus the `additionalProperties` list in `schema-validator`. `JSON.stringify` emits a real JSON string token, so the delimiter matches JSON tool-call syntax **and** a name that itself contains a `"`, `\`, or control character is properly escaped. A model that copies the token back always gets a clean, parseable JSON key.
- **Detectors, all five surfaces:** add one shared `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty(message, name)` helper co-located with the producer in `validation-errors.ts` that accepts both the legacy single-quoted and the new `JSON.stringify` wording, and route every version-fallback detector through it. The mirror of `JSON.stringify` on both the producer and the matcher keeps the escaping symmetric. `context-engine/registry.ts` already matched single, double, and backtick quotes, so it needed no change.

## Why this covers the whole issue (not one surface)

- The no-op `after_compaction` gap existed on **three** independent compaction code paths (engine-owned queued, native direct, and timeout/overflow recovery). Fixing only one would still hang on the others. All three are fixed and all three have regression coverage.
- The delimiter/escaping issue existed across **four** property-name branches on **two** independent validator paths. All four now route through `JSON.stringify`.
- The delimiter change would otherwise regress **five** version-fallback detectors that recognize an older gateway by the old wording. All five now accept both wordings through one shared matcher, so mixed-version `cron.list`, `connect`, `node.invoke`, `sessions.resolve`, and `sessions.usage` fallbacks keep firing, and each has both-wording retry coverage.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.timeout-triggered-compaction.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` -> compaction regression coverage passing (engine-skip no-op, engine default reason, native-skip paired-observer, timeout-recovery no-op, overflow-recovery no-op).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts` -> 56 passed (adds the `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` unit coverage plus the JSON-token validator assertions).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/gateway.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-resolution.test.ts` -> 223 passed (each version-fallback detector now parametrized over both wordings).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.test.ts` -> 5 passed (`sessions.usage` retry parametrized over both wordings).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: a no-op compaction now emits `after_compaction` (so a paired voice observer is not left waiting); both validators now format property names through `JSON.stringify` (so a tool-calling model always copies back a valid, parseable JSON key even when the property name contains a `"` or `\`); and every version-fallback detector that recognizes an older gateway rejecting an additive field now accepts both the legacy single-quoted and the new JSON-quoted wording, so the delimiter change does not silently break mixed-version fallbacks.

Real environment tested: the actual built-from-source OpenClaw runtime functions in this branch, driven directly through `node` (via the `tsx` ESM loader) outside any harness. Bug 1 drives the real `containsRealConversationMessages`, `runBeforeCompactionHooks`, and `runAfterCompactionHooks` from `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/`, with a real `registerInternalHook` voice-style observer. Bug 2 drives the real `formatValidationErrors` from `packages/gateway-protocol/` and the real `validateJsonSchemaValue` from `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts`. The detector proof drives the real shared `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` and the real `requestSessionsUsage` retry path from `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: register a paired `session:compact:before` / `session:compact:after` observer, feed a heartbeat-only transcript (so `containsRealConversationMessages` returns false, the real no-op trigger), then run the real before/after emission the patched no-op branch performs; feed a hostile property name containing an embedded quote and backslash into the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator, read back each formatted message, and parse the token a JSON model would copy back; then take the patched formatter's own JSON-quoted rejection, run it through both the old single-quoted matching form and the new shared matcher, and drive the real `requestSessionsUsage` against a gateway that rejects the additive `timeZone` field in each wording to observe whether the additive field is stripped and the call retried.

Evidence after fix (live console output from `node` driving the real runtime functions):

```
$ node --import tsx proof-bug1.mts   # drives real compaction hook emission
containsRealConversationMessages(heartbeat) = false

# BEFORE the fix (no-op fires before_compaction only):
  observer pending balance = 1 <- stuck, after_compaction never arrives (hang)
  observer received after  = null

# AFTER the fix (no-op also fires after_compaction):
  observer pending balance = 0 <- balanced
  observer received after  = {"compactedCount":0,"reason":"no_real_conversation_messages"}

$ node --import tsx proof-validator-escape.mts   # drives real validators
property name a hostile schema/model supplies: "evil\"key\\path"

# BEFORE (raw interpolation into hand-written double quotes):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\"key\\path\""
  token a model copies = "\"evil\"key\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = false

# AFTER (real gateway-protocol formatValidationErrors):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = true

# AFTER (real plugin schema-validator required-property miss):
  message = "must have required property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  contains a valid JSON string token? = true

$ node --import tsx proof-detector.mts   # drives real matcher + requestSessionsUsage retry
patched producer message = "invalid sessions.usage params: at root: unexpected property \"timeZone\""

# BEFORE (shipped detector: single-quoted includes only):
  matches patched producer output? = false  <- version fallback silently stops firing

# AFTER (shared messageReportsUnexpectedProperty, both wordings):
  matches legacy single-quoted rejection? = true
  matches JSON-quoted rejection?          = true

# real requestSessionsUsage retry against an older gateway:
  legacy single-quoted rejection -> stripped timeZone, retried (calls=2)
  JSON-quoted rejection          -> stripped timeZone, retried (calls=2)
  unrelated invalid-usage error   -> rethrown, not retried
```

Observed result after fix: the real no-op path now delivers `after_compaction` with `{compactedCount:0, reason:"no_real_conversation_messages"}` to the paired observer, returning its pending balance to 0 instead of hanging at 1; for a property name carrying an embedded quote and backslash, both the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator now emit a `JSON.stringify`-escaped token that round-trips through `JSON.parse` back to the original name; and the version-fallback detectors now recognize the patched validator's JSON-quoted rejection that the shipped single-quoted matcher missed, so the real `requestSessionsUsage` strips the additive `timeZone` field and retries against an older gateway in both wordings, while an unrelated invalid-usage error is still rethrown without a retry.

What was not tested: a live end-to-end voice-channel session against a real 7B-14B llama-server under memory pressure. This change is at the compaction-hook, validation-formatter, and version-fallback-detector layers, exercised above by driving the real runtime functions plus the regression coverage; a full hardware voice loop was out of scope for this environment.

Fixes #81925

target.title: fix(browser): normalize geolocation permission origins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users calling Browser `/set/geolocation` with a normal page URL in `origin`, such as `https://x.test/path`, did not get the same origin normalization as `/permissions/grant`, and malformed or `file://` origins were not rejected before the Playwright geolocation set path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Browser routes now share one HTTP(S) origin parser. `/set/geolocation` normalizes supplied origins to `URL.origin` before invoking Playwright and rejects non-HTTP(S) or malformed origins for geolocation set operations with the same error used by the dedicated permissions route.

The clear path intentionally returns before parsing `origin`, because clearing geolocation and permissions does not use an origin. This preserves existing clients that send stale or malformed origin fields while clearing state.

## User Impact

Users can pass page URLs as geolocation permission origins and get the expected site origin grant. Invalid local-file or malformed origins fail fast with a clear 400 response for set operations instead of reaching the browser mutation path. `clear=true` still clears geolocation even when an unused origin field is malformed.

## Evidence

Exact head: `4c82a884ebec97d3d4a22b79e072fdc9697a4c76`.

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 2 files / 25 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/origin.ts` passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/origin.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Proof

- The route-level `/set/geolocation` proof exercises the registered Browser route handler with the Playwright geolocation adapter mocked at the plugin boundary.
- It proves a supplied page URL, `https://geo.example/path?query=1#hash`, is normalized before the adapter call, and Playwright receives `origin: "https://geo.example"`.
- It proves `file:///tmp/page.html` and malformed set origins return 400 before tab resolution and before any Playwright geolocation call.
- It proves `clear=true` returns before parsing unused coordinates or origin, so malformed unused origin input cannot block geolocation clearing; the adapter receives `clear: true` for the selected tab.
- The sibling `/permissions/grant` route proof remains in the focused run to show the shared HTTP(S) origin parser keeps permission-origin behavior aligned.

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): reject malformed endpoints
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Malformed Microsoft Foundry base URLs could be treated as usable endpoints. `extractFoundryEndpoint()` called `normalizeFoundryEndpoint()` directly, and the fallback normalization path returned a trimmed string even when `new URL(...)` could not parse the value.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime endpoint extraction should only accept real HTTP(S) URLs. When a configured model endpoint is malformed, the provider should ignore that unusable value and continue to the existing metadata or environment fallback path instead of building provider URLs from invalid text.

## User Impact

Users with stale or malformed Foundry model base URLs can still recover through valid Entra profile metadata or endpoint fallback sources. Invalid configured endpoint strings no longer block a working Foundry configuration from being used.

## Evidence

The regression test covers a model with `baseUrl: "not a url"` and valid Entra profile metadata. Before this change, endpoint extraction treated the malformed string as present; after this change it returns `undefined` and runtime auth builds the base URL from the metadata endpoint.

## Proof

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=.vitest-cache-foundry-endpoint node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/index.test.ts`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/microsoft-foundry/shared.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/index.test.ts`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/microsoft-foundry/shared.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/index.test.ts`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude`

target.title: fix(plugins): keep API key preview from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the API-key preview shown during provider setup could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the pasted key contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`formatApiKeyPreview` used raw `String.prototype.slice` for its head and tail snippets, which can cut through surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the redacted preview always stays on valid UTF-16 boundaries. The change is limited to this display helper and its test.

## User Impact

Setup confirmation prompts and status output that display API-key previews remain well-formed when the key value contains non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests in `src/plugins/provider-auth-input.test.ts` covering ASCII redaction and astral boundary cases.
- Existing provider auth input tests continue to pass.
- Fixed a test callback that passed `Array.map`'s numeric index as the formatter's `opts` argument; it now uses an explicit unary wrapper.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, `formatApiKeyPreview("a😀b")` returned `"a\ud83d…\ude00b"` (isolated surrogate halves at both edges). After the patch it returns `"a…b"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/provider-auth-preview-utf16` at `c5ea197606ae06c8b1dc4700c2781667360cb5b8`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { formatApiKeyPreview } from "./src/plugins/provider-auth-input.ts"; for (const v of ["a😀b", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(20), "x".repeat(20) + "😀abc", "😀".repeat(10)]) console.log(JSON.stringify(formatApiKeyPreview(v)));'
  ```
  And to verify the previews survive a real disk round-trip without corrupting:

target.title: fix(imessage): apply authoritative projection in anchorless recovery
target.body:
Fixes openclaw/openclaw#104136

## What Problem This Solves

`repairIMessageConversationAnchor()` recovered conversation anchors from exact-GUID `messages.history` rows but only overlaid `chat_id` / `chat_guid` / `chat_identifier`. It preserved stale notification `sender`, `destination_caller_id`, and `is_from_me`, which could:

1. Route a direct reply at the local iMessage identity instead of the remote peer.
2. Dispatch an outgoing row as inbound when history says `is_from_me: true` but the broken notification said `false`.

## Changes

- Build a complete **authoritative recovery projection** from exact-GUID history rows (sender, direction, conversation fields).
- **Keep `destination_caller_id` optional** per imsg payload contract; when history omits it, **clear** any stale notification value.
- **Fail-closed** on incomplete/conflicting projections; **drop recovered `is_from_me: true` rows**.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `bb01b67d`

Rank-up: exact-GUID history now clears stale `destination_caller_id` when omitted (no longer inherits the broken notification value).

|-------|------|--------|
| L1 | issue synthetic repro: stale sender → authoritative remote sender | pass |
| L1 | history omits `destination_caller_id` → clears stale notification value | pass |

| L1 | conflicting exact-GUID rows | dropped |

target.title: fix(signal): align supported message actions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal's message-action adapter advertised support for every non-`send` action, but its handler only implements `react`. That meant unsupported actions like `delete` or `pin` could pass the ownership-boundary support check and then fail later inside the handler.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Signal adapter should advertise only the actions it can actually handle. `send` still stays on the normal outbound path, and reaction add/remove behavior remains represented by the existing `react` action parameters.

## User Impact

Unsupported Signal message actions are rejected earlier and consistently by the plugin action support contract. Existing Signal reactions continue to work, and send behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `extensions/signal/src/message-actions.ts` now returns `true` only for `react` in `supportsAction`.
- `extensions/signal/src/message-actions.test.ts` keeps the existing `send=false` / `react=true` assertions and adds `delete=false` / `pin=false` coverage.
- Current head also registers the real Signal plugin in the shared message-action dispatcher test registry and proves `delete` is declined at the dispatcher boundary while `react` still reaches the Signal reaction handler.

## Proof

- Dispatcher-boundary proof: `dispatchChannelMessageAction({ channel: "signal", action: "delete", ... })` returns `null` for an exact-current Signal conversation and does not call `sendReactionSignal` or `removeReactionSignal`.
- Reaction continuity proof: `dispatchChannelMessageAction({ channel: "signal", action: "react", ... })` returns `{ ok: true, added: "👍" }` and calls `sendReactionSignal("+15550001111", 123, "👍", { accountId: "work", ... })`.

target.title: fix(google-meet): guard node-host meet URLs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Google Meet chrome node-host command accepted any non-empty `start.url` before launching Chrome or starting realtime bridge processes. The higher-level node invoke policy already normalizes Meet URLs, but the node-host command is its own execution boundary and direct calls could still pass non-Meet URLs into local Chrome/bridge side effects.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves the existing Google Meet URL contract into a lightweight shared helper and applies it inside `startChrome` before any BlackHole check, audio bridge startup, or Chrome launch. `runtime.ts` continues to re-export `normalizeMeetUrl`, while `node-invoke-policy.ts` imports the same helper directly so the policy and host boundary cannot drift.

## User Impact

Invalid or non-Meet URLs now fail fast with the same stable Google Meet URL errors used by the runtime and node invoke policy. Valid `https://meet.google.com/...` meeting URLs keep the same launch, bridge, list, and stop behavior.

## Evidence

- `extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts` now normalizes `params.url` with the shared Meet URL contract before local side effects.
- `extensions/google-meet/node-host.test.ts` covers a non-Meet realtime start request and proves neither `spawnSync` nor child processes are reached.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/runtime.ts` re-exports the helper so existing callers that import from runtime remain compatible.
- Direct node-host proof on current head invoked `handleGoogleMeetNodeHostCommand()` with `action=start`, `mode=realtime`, `launch=true`, and a non-Meet URL. It returned the Meet URL contract error on Linux before any bridge session existed or was created.

## Proof

- Direct node-host transcript:

```text

before list: {"bridges":[]}
```

target.title: fix(cron): persist startup catch-up deferrals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102236. A startup overflow catch-up slot could be persisted to SQLite while its protection marker existed only in memory. Restarting again before that slot fired let maintenance advance the job to its next natural cron slot, silently losing the deferred run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferral marker now lives on `CronJobState` as `pendingCatchupDeferral`, so the existing `state_json` persistence and rollback paths own the slot and marker together. The process-local Set and its parallel rollback bookkeeping are removed. Maintenance clears the persisted marker when the slot arrives, when no valid deferred slot remains, or when the job is disabled; execution also clears it after an outcome. Existing rows need no migration because an absent field means no pending deferral.

## User Impact

Overflow system-event cron jobs keep their staggered startup catch-up run across repeated gateway restarts instead of silently skipping to the next natural schedule. Unrelated stale future cron slots are still repaired normally.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite restart path: one service starts and persists an overflow deferral, a fresh service starts 3 seconds later against the same store, the original 5-second slot survives, executes once, and clears its marker.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.startup-overflow-clobber.test.ts src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts src/cron/service/ops.test.ts`: 3 files, 107 tests passed.

target.title: fix(feishu): bound stalled docx image URL reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users rendering or uploading Feishu docx images from remote URLs could have the docx workflow hang when the remote image response body stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Docx image URL reads now go through a Feishu-local remote image reader that applies the selected account's Feishu HTTP timeout as two targeted deadlines: a response-header deadline and a response-body idle deadline. It no longer uses the setting as a complete-operation download deadline, so healthy large image transfers that keep making progress are not cut off solely because total elapsed time exceeds the header timeout. File upload remote reads keep their existing behavior, so this stays scoped to docx image handling.

## User Impact

Feishu docx image processing now degrades through the existing error handling instead of blocking the whole document operation on a stalled remote image body. Account-specific Feishu timeout settings are honored for docx image response headers and stalled body reads without changing the Feishu config schema.

Fixes an issue where Workboard claim authorization compared claim tokens with ordinary string equality. Claim tokens are redacted credentials that let a worker other than the recorded owner heartbeat, release, or mutate a claimed card, so their validation should use the same timing-safe primitive as other OpenClaw secret-bearing authorization surfaces.

## Why This Change Was Made

This covers both tool-level preflight checks and store-level heartbeat, release, and mutation enforcement without adding configuration or dependencies.

## User Impact

Workboard claim authorization now avoids data-dependent string comparison timing for claim tokens. Existing valid and invalid token behavior, error messages, and card workflows remain unchanged.

- The browser sent the SDP `POST` with the expected authorization/content-type headers and 9-byte offer body.
- The same-origin server sent response headers but kept the answer body open, reproducing the stalled answer-body case without CORS/private-network interference.
- The Control UI realtime state machine left connecting state after ~30s, closed the peer without setting a remote description, stopped the media track, and ended in `realtimeTalkStatus="error"` with `realtimeTalkActive=false`.
- Chromium surfaces this abort as `The user aborted a request.` rather than the custom timeout message; the fake-timer unit test still verifies the custom abort reason on the lower-level transport path.
- Not run: live OpenAI Realtime API / real microphone permission prompt / screenshot or video artifact.

AI-assisted change.

target.title: [Bug]: embedded prompt cache breaks across room-event, policy, and Responses boundaries
target.body:
## Summary

Long-lived embedded sessions can lose provider prompt-cache reuse when adjacent turns cross room-event delivery, authorization, queue, compaction, recovery, or native Responses continuation boundaries.

Sanitized same-session traces showed model-visible tool inventory changing between 44 and 47 tools, prompt/tool digests changing with it, and cached prefixes collapsing to roughly 2k-10k tokens or plateauing around 37k-40k.

After stabilizing request shape, numeric-only records from a long-lived room session show the cached prefix growing from 104,960 to 157,184 tokens; the final four turns reused 98.7-99.2% of the input prefix. Exact-head isolated live-provider probes then reused 40,960 cached tokens on warm GPT-5.5 turns (99.5%) and 40,448 on warm GPT-5.6 turns (98.2-98.3%), with one stable 48-tool ordered shape digest. No transcript text or private identifiers are included.

## Root Cause

Three independent concerns were coupled:

1. turn-specific delivery and authorization changed reusable prompt/tool definitions;
2. reconstructed queue, memory, compaction, fallback, and recovery runs could lose authoritative state;
3. built-in authenticated OpenAI Responses streams could miss native `previous_response_id` continuation.

## Expected Contract

- One stable model-visible prompt and ordered tool catalogue for a session.
- One deterministic, trusted current-turn `ToolAccessPolicy` enforced before side effects.
- Trusted-internal capability remains distinct from owner identity, so limited core-tool grants cannot expose owner-only plugin tools.
- Actual reply routing remains turn-specific without changing prompt-facing tool shape.
- Queue, memory, compaction, provider, and recovery boundaries preserve the same state.
- Authenticated GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 Responses use native continuation; custom streams retain their routing.
- Supervised Codex turns keep native model/effort/personality settings while receiving trusted turn guidance through append-only developer history.

## Candidate Fix

PR #102189 at `b0a9bfc589f8deff1ed9dd5345276093d6df25b2` implements the contract above.

The candidate includes upstream `7027d2c227281d814266311bebab7581b899d6dc` and has a clean merge-tree check against it. Pre-refresh broad validation passed 2,446 changed-file tests plus focused trusted-internal ownership, compaction, overflow recovery, harness selection, and manual propagation coverage. Exact-head validation passes 14 proof assertions across 18 suites, 215 Codex lifecycle/binding/login-profile tests, production typecheck, prompt snapshots, diff checks, and a full build.

An exact-head focused proof run passes 14 selected assertions across 18 suites: strict room-event delivery, pre-hook/pre-side-effect denial, permitted trusted-internal execution, and GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 `previous_response_id` delta continuation.

The exact commit is installed on the reporter's local gateway: OpenClaw `2026.7.2`, LaunchAgent loaded, runtime active, connectivity probe OK, dashboard HTTP 200, Discord probe OK, WhatsApp linked/healthy, and build-info commit matches the candidate.

## Privacy

Evidence is intentionally sanitized. No private sender, channel, account, host, endpoint, credential, or raw trace identifiers are included.

Disclaimer: This issue was filed and updated autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter.
